projects.title: Broken Tiles Material
projects.description: Broken tile material made within designer created for a personal project
projects.heroAlt: 4k Broken Tile Render In Unreal Engine
projects.mainText: This broken tile material was created to push my knowledge and abilities to the extent, I wanted to create a material outside from a university assignment on my own time whilst being able to do what I want with full creative freedom.

sections.alt: I create a base tileable mask, I chose this shape as I personally thought it was an interesting shape and I had an idea with the painted on design ontop of the final material using this shape

I wanted to have missing and cracked tiles on this material, therefore due to how thin these tiles would be in real life they would crack in a more glass-like way where they would crack and shatter within their cracks this also allows for a better visual, I created cells that simulated broken edges and within certain crack islands I would crack it more by masking out random cells and combining it with a lower sized crack mask
merged together the mask functions pretty well the cracks dont run through the entire shape and each tile has its own unique crack masked out so it doesnt affect every tile within the mask.

I make the gradient for my tiles in a way that would show a physical hit, I deepen the tiles to show an impact happened within that spot and in the highest density of damage is where the breaks point, I also added a random tilt to a minor amount of tiles due to the fact not every tile would do that in a real material.
due to the scale of the project I make sure to create my masks that will be reused such as my floodfills to a wireless node, I also create a mask that removes broken tiles at random from my material

I add a large amount of minor noise and minor damage to the tiles to add chaos, which makes a better final visual product this is seen in real life mostly and its a great way to make more photorealistic materials

after doing construction work for a long time within my life, I saw a fine grout done for ceramic tiles which I wanted replicated for my material, I create a tileable cross material and mask it out for damage and so it elevates where the tiles are not present, there was an issue where sometiems the grout would grow over the tiles but after some masking and tweaks this issue was solved promptly
I created a pebble generator to disperse broken shards of tile in the cracks and missing areas of the tile material with larger shards being placed closer to the non-missing tiles
The coloring of the tiles and grout was made to mimic my reference image,

This large spline system was to create this pattern for my material, I would have love to create this pattern in way less nodes but due to the limitation of the spline node this massive list was what I needed to create this pattern
I used the pattern to create this spline system that makes brushstrokes in my material, it is applied subtly but adds alot of information that makes the tiles look painted by hand.
This tiles and applies a fade away for the paint and works with the tileabiltiy of my material

projects.title: Emberline
projects.description: Shapes, silhouettes and a language of heat for a world at the edge of collapse.
projects.lede: Shapes, silhouettes and a language of heat for a world at the edge of collapse.
projects.mainText: Emberline began with a question: how can a landscape communicate danger before a single character appears? I explored compressed compositions, hot colour accents and heavy atmospheric perspective to make the environment feel active and unstable.

projects.title: Liminal Gardens
projects.description: A quiet exploration of overgrown architecture, soft light and the stories left behind.
projects.lede: A quiet exploration of overgrown architecture, soft light and the stories left behind.
projects.mainText: Liminal Gardens is a visual development project about places that have been reclaimed by time. The brief was to create an environment that felt both welcoming and slightly unknowable, using a restrained palette and strong architectural silhouettes.

projects.title: Mossy Brick Material
projects.description: A mossy brick material made within Substance Designer and rendered in Unreal Engine using a dynamic material system.
projects.mainText:
I created this material for my emergent games module in university, where I went to do a mastery project on node based materials, materials are a huge passion of mine and i have been doing node based materials since i picked up Blender in 2020, thoughout the years my understanding and talent in material creation have allowed me to create materials that are near-photorealistic. 

In turn I wanted to create a material system for a mossy brick material that mimiced a wall within the University campus.

sections.caption: The reference wall had this long bring short brick pattern of which was what made the wall interesting and in turn a interesting base shape, an individual tilt and randomness to each brick has been added to give it an imperfect look.
I break the bricks and give them shape changes, I also give them each a gradient to isolate them in the future.
Holes, Cracks, Scratches and Brick Depth are present within heavily damaged bricks

To make the moss look realistic the moss grows using light detail of the material's heighmap, which disperses the moss with the strongest form of it placed on the parts of the brick that would be seen in real brick.

I make bird excrement on my material look realistic by using shape details within the material to affect the bird excrement, along with effects that make the excrement look like it fell on with velocity and spalttered.

projects.title: Orbital Bloom
projects.description: System-led visual design for an optimistic science-fiction garden in the sky.
projects.lede: System-led visual design for an optimistic science-fiction garden in the sky.
projects.mainText:
Orbital Bloom is an art direction study for a future where growing things is a collective act. The work focused on defining a modular visual system that could move between intimate plant life and enormous orbital structures.

I created the colour script, shape language, environment keys and reference framework for the project.
